purpose: Prevent visual regression caused by repeatedly reconstructing an already-successful image from prose, changing passed dimensions while repairing a failed one, or abandoning previously proven execution routes.

authority_boundary.scope: Current VPD project execution control only.

core_invariants.rule: When an actual accepted or best-so-far visual asset exists, that asset is the primary visual authority. A prose prompt, summary, distilled rule, or recreated description may not substitute for the asset.

When the user identifies a result as best-so-far but does not explicitly call it final, preserve it as BEST_SO_FAR_PROTECTED. Further exploration must use sibling variants and must not overwrite the protected asset.

Human acceptance is scoped to the dimension actually accepted. If layout and wordmark pass but photography fails, freeze layout and wordmark and leave only photography open. Do not reinterpret a local fail as permission to redesign passed dimensions.

After any dimension is frozen, the next iteration may modify only the explicitly open failing dimension or target node(s). A full-image rerender or full-layout rebuild is prohibited unless the user explicitly reopens the frozen dimensions.
Do not recreate a protected master from text when the real pixel asset is available. Prefer exact asset reuse, layer replacement, masks, local edits, or sibling variants anchored to the master.

Keep the protected pixel master/reference intact and addressable. Production experiments must be created in sibling nodes/frames or reversible target layers. Destructive overwrite of the canonical master is prohibited.
If a candidate improves the open dimension but degrades any frozen dimension, reject that candidate and return to the frozen baseline. Do not continue repairing from the degraded candidate.
A visual change is not evidence of improvement. Promotion requires direct comparison against the protected baseline and, when the user is the human gate, actual-pixel human review.
Keep one explicitly open visual problem per iteration whenever possible. Do not simultaneously optimize unrelated dimensions because that destroys causal attribution and increases drift.

Before inventing or retrying an execution path, read the current task lock and proven route evidence. If a route is already verified, reuse it. A new route is allowed only after a specific verified failure of the existing route.

Record asset identity/provenance for protected and candidate states where available: file reference, generation id, Figma frame/node ids, image hash, SHA-256, human verdict, and exact frozen/open dimensions.

Do not silently create many hidden alternatives after a master is protected. Default to one visible candidate per open-problem iteration unless the current task lock explicitly authorizes another budget.

The human-confirmed mushroom photographic-realism Golden must remain addressable as an actual-pixel evaluation benchmark. Future photographic candidates intended to support quality, migration, promotion or baseline claims must pass the absolute obvious-AI regression gate before relative A/B mechanism wins count as success. The Golden is an evaluation anchor by default, not an additional runtime generation reference.

human_verdict_mapping.ambiguity_rule: If scope is ambiguous, preserve the existing best asset and do not infer permission to overwrite passed dimensions.

allowed: Create at most one visible photography-repair candidate.
Change only PHOTO_BASE_CLEAN 201:3 or create a sibling photo candidate for comparison.
Keep all frozen design nodes unchanged.
Show the integrated full poster to the user for actual-pixel review.
Promote the photo only if the user says the AI-feel problem is materially improved without harming the accepted design.
prohibited: Rebuild the accepted composition from prompt text.
Change the accepted wordmark while fixing photography.
Change support hierarchy while fixing photography.
Treat a merely different photo as an automatic improvement.
Retry a solved upload route from scratch.
